FABLE — BEB-7496 CORRECTED. Alex: the brand is linked to the FRAG, which is for the PLUGIN, which is linked to the AUTHOR'S COMPANY that made the plugin.

I had the subject set as {site, listing} — that is the client half only. The second chain is the one the marketplace and the author economics run on:

**author company → plugin → frag**

The brand belongs to the author's company. The plugin carries it. The frag inherits it. In the marketplace, in the exploded view, in a config kit, in directory linking — the brand a person sees is the PLUGIN AUTHOR'S, not ours and not the client's.

That is what makes the ability-factory work (BEB-1423): we build the frag, publish with the author as author, reach out for the claim. A frag not carrying the author's own brand gives them nothing recognisable to claim and no reason to cross-promote us.

**FOUR SUBJECT TYPES, ONE SCHEMA:** site (domain) · listing (gers_id) · author company · plugin.
A FRAG GETS NO BRAND RECORD OF ITS OWN. It RESOLVES through its plugin to that plugin's author company, at read time — so an author updating their brand updates every frag of theirs at once. A frag holding a copied brand is the drift failure again.

**BOTH BLOCKING QUESTIONS CHANGE:**
Q1 the R2 key must express subject TYPE. "tenant + domain" cannot address a plugin author who is not a tenant of ours — and until they claim, they are not one. The key has to hold an UNCLAIMED author company's brand.
Q3 NEW AND BLOCKING — what happens to the brand ON CLAIM? 1423's model is residuals accruing to Alex until the author claims. Same shape here and never ruled: before claim we have harvested their brand without them. Who owns that record meanwhile, what may it appear on, and does claiming replace it or confirm it? Nobody guesses this — it touches someone else's marks.

Resolution order for a frag: plugin's author company, else named ABSENT. NEVER fall back to abilifi's brand silently — an unbranded frag must look unbranded, not look like ours.
